Scope: arterial and local roads, potable water, sewage, storm drainage, irrigation, street lighting and telecom networks, sewage pump stations and storm drainage ponds for Phase 1, Part 2 of the 3rd Industrial City in Dammam.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours. This week the weekly report moved to a new measure taken from MODON's revised schedule (2,336,000 budgeted labour units, including engineering, procurement and testing). At the 08-Nov-2026 data date the project is 42.2% complete against 56.0% planned, 13.8% behind plan. These figures cannot be compared with last week's 77.6% against 96.6%, so no weekly gain can be shown.

The P6 update now finishes the project 169 days late. The contractor's P6 update (data date 07-Nov-2026) schedules project finish on 03-Nov-2027, 169 days after the contract completion date of 18-May-2027 and 7 days later than last week, with −168 days of float; the weekly report still forecasts 18-May-2027. To finish on the contract date, the remaining 57.8% needs about 2.14% a week over the 27 whole weeks left. The weakest areas are the Zone 1 sewage network (29.1% against 58.7% planned), the potable water networks in Zones 2 and 3, and pre-testing and testing (30.7% against 45.5%).

Site photos this week

Six photo sheets uploaded with this week's report, dated 1 to 3 November 2026 by the contractor. Work centred on potable water valves and fire hydrants, a flow test of the storm water manholes, the sewer force main at Lift Station 1 and the concrete encasement of the telecom ducts. The schedules uploaded this week disagree on completion. The contractor's P6 update (1,255 activities, data date 07-Nov-2026) finishes on 03-Nov-2027, 7 days later than last week's 27-Oct-2027. MODON's revised schedule "MDD-Update 78" (2,970 activities, data date 09-Nov-2026), which carries the new physical measure, finishes on 18-May-2027 with no float to spare and the revised-scope works on 03-Apr-2027. A third, 136-activity revised schedule (data date 07-Nov-2026) finishes on 26-Jun-2027, 39 days late. The P6 export in the weekly report's Milestones sheet shows 11-Jul-2027, and the weekly report itself forecasts 18-May-2027.

Procurement of key materials

Share of total quantity delivered to site for the long-lead items. Source: weekly presentation 10-Nov-2026, long-lead items slide.

Pumps: 2 of 15 deliveredGrundfos pump accessories are being installed at the stations, but only 2 pumps have arrived because of global shipping problems; no pump or panel was delivered this week. The water station control panel (IGEC, 1 set) and sewage station panels (WAMCO, 4 sets) are not expected in full until January 2027; the control system target is 28-Jan-2027.
Generators and surge vesselsThe two generators (Kohler – Abunayyan) are in the Kingdom and wait for the factory and site acceptance tests before delivery to site. Surge vessel deliveries (7) are now expected to start around 28-Nov-2026, moved again from 05-Nov-2026. The VEGA supplier has given no delivery date. The water pump maintenance (SPP) now expects its parts on 24-Nov-2026.

Labour has fallen from 397 in March–April to 332; the issue log names low manpower and productivity as a cause of delay. The presentation lists 114 items of equipment working on site.

Open issues and risks

Saudi Electricity work permitsContractor / Consultant / OwnerNew this week: the Saudi Electricity Company has suspended issuing the remaining work permits, which directly delays the handover of the works. The project manager visited the company; support from MODON and the consultant is needed. Status: on hold.
Pond 4ContractorMODON approved the proposal. Work starts after the sewer network at the junction of Road 25 and Road 9; target moved again to 19-Nov-2026 (was 14-Nov-2026).
Road 25 crossingsContractorPart one of the Road 25 / Road 2 junction is done and part two is being prepared; it needs asphalt cutting for phases 1 and 2 once the city administration approves a traffic diversion. At Road 25 / Road 9, approval of pipe jacking for the sewer line is awaited; target 15-Nov-2026.
Permits on Roads 25 and 1Consultant / OwnerPermit issue is suspended on Roads 25 and 1 and some works there are still stopped. Permits were requested and submitted; awaiting approval.
Block F and Road 9Consultant / OwnerWorks in Block F stopped from 06-Oct-2026 until power is connected to the Chinese factory. Work on Road 9 in area F is banned (partial stop) despite an approved permit.
Sewer manholes and box culvertConsultant / Owner22 sewer manholes have connections that clash with the storm water box culvert, blocking pipe connections. The contractor's proposal is to be reviewed by the consultant and sent to the owner; the 05-Nov-2026 target has passed.
Telecom manholes and Ansab officesConsultantNew this week: 2 telecom manholes clash with the Ansab offices. The consultant is coordinating with Ansab and the contractor; consultant's response due 09-Nov-2026.
Pump station equipmentContractorGenerators, surge vessels and pumps are paid and being manufactured; 2 sewage pumps and the fire pumps have been delivered (target 30-Nov-2026). Water pump maintenance has a purchase order; target 15-Nov-2026.
Third-party interfacesConsultant / OwnerSlab settlement caused by Watco and Al-Issa works: several meetings held, no response from Al-Issa. The Al-Issa office gate conflicts with a lighting pole foundation.
Network testingContractorTesting is needed so complete networks can be handed over. The test plan was merged into the corrective plan submitted on 08-Nov-2026; testing is under way.
Manpower and productivityContractorLow manpower and equipment and low productivity of the contractor's own crews (MODON issue log, high priority). Excavation is done by hand because there are no records of the existing services.

The MODON risk register was rewritten this week: lower cash flow for the contractor because the contract value was reduced (high), delays in long-lead supplies from regional and global shipping problems (high), disagreement between the consultant and MODON over the contractor's financial claims (high), work stoppages without prior notice after a change in the permit process (medium), and stoppages on permitted Roads 25, 1 and 9 (medium).

Data notes

  • This-week values compare with the 03-Nov-2026 upload in the W06 folder. The list of major activities in the Photos - Progress Summary sheet is unchanged again, the manpower and issues sheets carry no new figures, and the procurement log is still the 20-Oct-2026 file.
  • The report week is the contract week stated in the Milestones sheet ("Current Contract Weeks: 77 of 104"); (08-Nov-2026 − 19-May-2025) ÷ 7 gives 76 whole weeks, as contract weeks count from 1. The workbook calls itself report #65, and its file name carries 11-10-2026 (10-Nov-2026, month first) although its data date is 08-Nov-2026.
  • The physical measure changed this week. It now comes from MODON's revised schedule "MDD-Update 78" (2,970 activities, data date 09-Nov-2026): 2,336,000 budgeted labour units split in fixed shares of 3% engineering, 27% procurement, 10% pre-testing and testing and 60% construction. Last week's measure counted construction man-hours only (458,486 to 467,288). The two cannot be compared, so no weekly gain is shown. The chart sheet gives 38.2% at the end of October and 42.2% at 9 November on the new basis, but no weekly figure.
  • Within construction, each zone's and network's physical % is identical to its value-weighted % in the same sheet, so the construction labour units appear to be spread in proportion to cost rather than estimated from man-hours. The 42.2% should be confirmed with the contractor.
  • Earned labour units differ slightly: 984,762 (42.16%) in the Weekly Progress Report sheet against 986,227 (42.22%) in the chart sheet and the presentation.
  • Weekly Progress Report sheet errors: the Construction row counts the zones twice (143.9% planned, 104.9% earned); the Zone 2 main road row is labelled "Main Road Zone 1"; the Zone 3 main road shows no earned units against 99.9% planned although its value progress is shown nearly complete; the Zone 3 sewage network now carries only 244 units (under 0.1%) after 7.6% of the man-hours last week.
  • The chart sheet's baseline equals the actual curve up to October 2026 and then plans 31.3% for November alone. Its revised-plan column is still on last week's 467,280 man-hour basis, so it is not shown; the forecast column is shown instead.
  • Completion dates disagree: weekly report 18-May-2027; MDD-Update 78 18-May-2027; 136-activity revised schedule 26-Jun-2027; P6 export in the Milestones sheet 11-Jul-2027; contractor's P6 update 03-Nov-2027. The P6 update still leaves milestones 3 and 4 (work plan, drawings approval) not started, while the weekly report and presentation show them complete. The Schedule sheet's activity counts (543 not started, 334 in progress, 378 completed) do not match the P6 update file (345, 422, 488).
  • The presentation slides 3, 4 and 5 and the earned value columns of the workbook report value-weighted (cost-based) progress labelled as achieved; those figures are not used in this report.
  • Contract value: the weekly report gives a revised value of 146,170,171 SAR and a saving scope of 69,605,906 SAR; the presentation gives a current project value of 164,170,171 SAR and a saving of 69,405,562 SAR. The original value is 233,776,077 SAR in the weekly report and 233,575,734 SAR in the presentation.
  • Invoices: the weekly report jumped from 12 invoices (37.3M SAR, to 15-Jul-2026) to 14 invoices (65.1M SAR, to 30-Sep-2026). Executed work not yet invoiced is 13,310,176 SAR on presentation slide 5 but 21,210,309 SAR on slide 2.
  • FIRs: the weekly report still shows 6,367 issued, 6,299 closed and 68 open, unchanged from last week; the presentation shows 6,426, 6,362 and 64.
  • Manpower: the summary panel still shows 388 labour and 57 staff (445), while the monthly table and the presentation show 332 labour and 66 staff (398) for November.
  • Scope quantities: the network quantities slide is empty this week, so all items come from the progress scope slide, which gives 2,839 m of potable water and 21,318 m of telecom duct against the 2,992 m and 64,321 m used last week from the network slide. The slide gives no unit for street lighting (pipe lengths are taken as metres, as on last week's network slide); storm water ponds are shown only as 93%.
